chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Rifah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever dies with no patron (mawla) and no heirs is among the people of this verse: “They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger.”'

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: The spoils or unique assets belonging to Allah and the Messenger
key_terms.قُلِ الْأَنْفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ: Say: The spoils are for Allah and the Messenger
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Patron or guardian in the context of inheritance

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of a person who dies with no heirs and no patron in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the inheritance of the heirless (gharim) to Quran 8:1, establishing that the spoils (anfal) belong to Allah and the Messenger. In Shia jurisprudence, this verse is interpreted to mean that the Imam, as the inheritor of the Prophet, assumes the role of the state treasury (bayt al-mal) to distribute the estate of one who has no kin or patron. This ruling highlights the theological continuity of authority from the Prophet to the Imams in matters of divine property.
